entry.title: Feature Request: Improve Pod Status Not Ready When all Containers Are Not Ready
entry.summary:
@kubernetes/sig-cli-feature-requests
# Feature Request: Improve Pod Status Not Ready When all Containers Are Not Ready
## Summary
I would like to propose improving the human-readable Pod status displayed by `kubectl get pods` when a Pod has multiple containers and one or more containers are not yet ready.
## Current behavior
For a Pod containing an application container and a sidecar container, the output may look like this:
```text NAME READY STATUS my-application-pod 1/2 Running ```
In this situation, the sidecar may be ready while the application container is still initializing or is not ready to serve requests. The `STATUS` column displays `Running`, which can give operators an incomplete picture when monitoring multiple Pods.
## Proposed behavior
Consider making the displayed status more descriptive when not all containers are ready.
For example:
```text NAME READY STATUS my-application-pod 1/2 NotReady ```
Alternatively, the status could reflect the specific startup condition:
```text NAME READY STATUS my-application-pod 0/2 ContainerCreating ```
The exact status names and transition rules would be subject to community discussion.
## Expected benefits
- Make partially initialized or unhealthy workloads easier to identify. - Improve operational visibility when monitoring Pods across multiple namespaces. - Reduce ambiguity between a Pod whose containers are running and a Pod whose containers are all ready. - Help operators identify application startup failures more quickly, particularly in multi-container Pods with sidecars.
## Compatibility considerations
I propose keeping the existing Pod phase semantics and API fields backward-compatible. Any enhancement should preferably improve the human-readable status presented by `kubectl` without introducing unnecessary changes to the Kubernetes Pod lifecycle API.
## Request for feedback
Would the Kubernetes community consider a change to the human-readable Pod status so that it more clearly distinguishes fully ready Pods from Pods with containers that are still starting or are not ready?

entry.title: Show Pod extended resource requests in kubectl describe node
entry.summary:
### Enhancement Description
- One-line enhancement description (can be used as a release note): Show Pod extended resource requests and limits in a separate table in `kubectl describe node`. - Kubernetes Enhancement Proposal: [Draft KEP PR #6473](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6473). - Discussion Link: SIG discussion has not taken place yet. Related prior work: [kubernetes/kubernetes#44271](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/44271) and [kubernetes/kubernetes#46079](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/46079). - PRs by stage and milestone: - [ ] Provisional design; no release target - [ ] KEP (`k/enhancements`) update PR: https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6473 - [ ] Code (`k/k`) update PR: not started - [ ] Docs (`k/website`) update PR: not started
The current node description shows extended resource totals but does not show which Pods requested them. This proposal adds one row per nonzero Pod/resource pair and reuses the existing Pod reads and resource calculations. Resource names come from Pod data; there is no vendor list.
A Pod may request several resource types, for example GPU count, memory, cores, and network resources. The table grows in rows rather than columns and does not silently truncate matching requests.
This differs from [KEP-5677](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/5677-dra-resource-availability-visibility), which adds an API and controller for DRA pool availability. This proposal shows scalar requests, including extended resource keys served by DRA, but does not expand explicit ResourceClaims. A note marks that limit when listed Pods reference Claims. It does not report device assignments or runtime use.
Proposed ownership is SIG CLI, with SIG Node participation. SIG sponsorship, the output design, and the release plan are not agreed yet. No new API, API calls, permissions, feature gate, or command-line flag is proposed.
/sig cli /sig node

entry.title: Show init container waiting reasons in Pod table output
entry.summary:
### Enhancement Description
- One-line enhancement description: Show the existing `PodInitializing` waiting reason alongside the init count in the server-generated Pod Table used by `kubectl get pods`. - Kubernetes Enhancement Proposal: [KEP PR #6468](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6468), status `provisional`; [proposed README](https://github.com/panpan0000/enhancements/blob/kep-6467-init-container-startup-status/keps/sig-node/6467-init-container-startup-status/README.md). - Discussion links: [original feature request](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/141686), [implementation PR](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141693), and [KEP-first guidance](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141693#issuecomment-6126926630). - Primary contact: @panpan0000 - Proposed owning SIG: SIG Node; participating SIG: SIG CLI. The printer-only scope requests SIG CLI review; ownership, sponsorship, and approvers remain to be confirmed. - PRs by stage and milestone: - [ ] Alpha - candidate Kubernetes v1.39 release; release stages subject to SIG agreement - [ ] KEP (`k/enhancements`) update PR(s): https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/6468 - [ ] Code (`k/k`) update PR(s): https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/141693 (earlier kubelet proposal; needs a separate printer-only update) - [ ] Docs (`k/website`) update PR(s): TBD
The scope is the server-side Pod printer and its tests. The API already separates `state.waiting` from `state.running`. A selected init waiting with `PodInitializing` displays `Init:N/M PodInitializing`; specific errors retain their current display. Kubelet status generation and Pod API fields remain unchanged. No feature gate is proposed. The display does not distinguish image pulling from container creation, and a count alone is not proof of running.
[KEP-5334: Image Pull Progress](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5334) addresses a related need through streaming progress APIs. This proposal is narrower and does not depend on those APIs. SIG CLI and SIG Node review of the printer scope is requested.
/sig node /sig cli

The Work API was accepted by SIG-Multicluster in 2021 and is implemented in https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/work-api, but the design has been updated. For example, the `AppliedWork` which has been discussed and agreed upon in the SIG-MC community https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/work-api/pull/14/changes and https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/work-api/pull/29 in 2023.
Every other SIG-MC APIs has its KEP created and maintained. The Work API is the one exception, which means there is no path to link to and no normal place to land design updates.
This Work KEP would migrate the original proposal into the KEP template, reconcile it with the current API and implementation. **It is not proposing changes to the API itself.**

entry.title: SLM: Coordinate Node lifecycle condition writers
entry.summary:
### Enhancement Description [Node lifecycle conditions](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/node/node-lifecycle-conditions/) provide a shared place to publish important lifecycle state, but the Condition API does not provide coordination semantics. Multiple actors, like admins running `kubectl drain`, remediation controllers, Node Problem Detector, infrastructure operators, ect., can all observe the same Node and independently decide to write lifecycle state invalidating each other.
**Problem** Node Condition writers are unaware of one another, so they can overwrite another actor's lifecycle signal or trigger conflicting remediation. There isn't an available way to coordinate who set the condition, how long it will be set for, ect..
**Goal** This KEP will define a coordination mechanism for Node lifecycle condition writers and a way to discover ownership. The mechanism should allow an actor to declare that it is managing a Node lifecycle operation, identify the scope of that ownership, and give other writers and readers enough structured context to avoid conflicting updates. It will also define how readers should interpret lifecycle state when an owner is present.
- One-line enhancement description (can be used as a release note): Add coordination mechanism for actors writing Node lifecycle conditions. - Kubernetes Enhancement Proposal: TBD - Discussion Link: - Use cases doc: [Node Lifecycle Coordination Using Conditions](https://docs.google.com/document/d/12nMG9Yyzd5D8iams5Oc4BEtfupe-li-Kxsxm_G7D_Ts/edit?usp=sharing) - [KEP-5683: Node Lifecycle Conditions](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-node/5683-lifecycle-conditions) - [Specialized Lifecycle Management](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5683) - [SLM: Publish kubectl drain state as Node conditions](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/6251) - [kubernetes/node-problem-detector#1176](https://github.com/kubernetes/node-problem-detector/issues/1176) - [kubernetes/node-problem-detector#457](https://github.com/kubernetes/node-problem-detector/issues/457) - PRs by stage and milestone: - [ ] Alpha - TBD - [ ] KEP (`k/enhancements`) update PR(s): - [ ] Code (`k/k`) update PR(s): - [ ] Docs (`k/website`) update PR(s):
